sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Barron County, WI?
sections.html:
Deeds for Barron County property are recorded by the county Register of Deeds, which holds the county's real estate records and its vital records. The office is listed under departments on the Barron County website.

The office describes its job as protecting the official county repository of real estate records and keeping it open to the public. One line on that page matters to sellers: the Register of Deeds office does not provide services for real estate searches. Order any title search through your title company or closing agent, and use the register only to record.

Under s. 59.43, the register records each document offered that the law does not bar, stamps it with the date, hour and minute, and takes documents in the order they arrive.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Barron County?
sections.html:
Recording most documents in Barron County costs $30, a flat fee set by state law in s. 59.43(2)(ag). Fees are payable in advance by whoever is asking for the service.

The rest of the state schedule is short:

  • $30 for a deed, mortgage, satisfaction or other document entitled to be recorded.
  • $50 for a cemetery plat, subdivision plat or condominium plat.
  • $2 for the first page of a copy and $1 for each added page.
  • $1 more to certify a copy.

The county's register page links to a Recording and Filing Fee Schedule hosted by the Wisconsin Register of Deeds Association. It also says recorded real estate documents come back only if you supply a self-addressed stamped envelope for a paper copy or an email address for a PDF. Put one or the other in the packet.

sections.h2: How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Barron County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays 30 cents for each $100 of value, which is $3 per $1,000, on any taxable deed (s. 77.22). At the county's median owner-occupied home value of $216,600 from the Census Bureau, the fee comes to $649.80.

Value means the full price paid or to be paid, including any liens. On a land contract it is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay. The register collects the fee when the deed is submitted, and both seller and buyer sign the return. The register has no duty to check your value or your exemption claim, so the accuracy of both rests with the people who sign. The county keeps 20 percent of the fee and the rest goes to the state (s. 77.24).

The Department of Revenue now takes the Real Estate Transfer Return through My Tax Account. Its RETR overview lists what you need before starting:

  • The completed deed.
  • Name, address, phone and email for each seller and buyer.
  • A Social Security number, ITIN or FEIN for each party.
  • The parcel numbers from the property tax bill.

After you submit, print the receipt and bring it with the notarized deed and payment. The overview says some counties accept this packet electronically, so ask the Barron County office which way it prefers. A transfer that spans two counties needs a separate return for each. If the department finds the value understated by 25 percent or more, or an exemption claimed wrongly, the penalty is $25 or 25 percent of the added fee, whichever is greater. Questions go to RETR@wisconsin.gov or 608-264-6885.

sections.h2: Which Barron County transfers owe no transfer fee?
sections.html:
A deed owes no fee only if it fits one of the exemptions in s. 77.25, and the deed itself must name the subsection that applies. The most common ones for home transfers are these:

  • Transfers by will, descent or survivorship.
  • Gifts or nominal-price transfers between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild.
  • Transfers between spouses.
  • A foreclosure, or a deed in lieu of foreclosure, to the mortgage holder.
  • Real estate worth $1,000 or less.
  • A deed that corrects or confirms an earlier recorded conveyance for nominal or no consideration.

The state treats exemptions narrowly. If the return does not offer the exemption you expected, the DOR guide says the transfer is subject to the fee.

sections.h2: How must a deed be formatted for Barron County to accept it?
sections.html:
A deed needs to meet the standard document format in s. 59.43(2m), or the register may refuse it. The checklist posted by the Wisconsin Register of Deeds Association restates the rules. In short:

  • Leave the upper right corner of page one blank for at least 3 by 3 inches, for the recording stamp.
  • Put the document title within the top 6 inches and return information on page one.
  • List the parcel identification number for every parcel the document affects.
  • Use white paper of at least 20 pound weight, 8.5 inches wide and 11 or 14 inches long, with pages not hinged.
  • Print in black, blue or red ink, with a top margin of half an inch and other margins of a quarter inch.
  • Show the name of whoever drafted the document, and type or print the grantor, grantee and notary names clearly.

The association's checklist adds that original signatures must be notarized or authenticated and that the transfer return and fee or exemption number must accompany the deed. A Social Security number on a document is a separate problem: under s. 59.43(1m) a register may not record a document that contains one. If a group of related documents is marked as one transaction and any one fails, the register may return the whole group unrecorded.

sections.h2: Can you record electronically in Barron County?
sections.html:
Yes. The county keeps a page of trusted e-recording submitters, and five vendors appear on it: CSC eRecording, EPN (Erecording Partners Network), Indecomm Global Service, Simplifile (a division of ICE Mortgage Technology) and Hopdox.

Ask your closing agent whether the file will go through one of these channels or arrive on paper, and confirm the Barron County register will accept it that way before signing day.

sections.h2: What is Barron County like for people selling a house?
sections.html:
Barron County is a mostly rural Wisconsin county with four cities: Barron (the county seat), Chetek, Cumberland and Rice Lake. It was created in 1859 as Dallas County, renamed Barron County in 1869 and organized in 1874. U.S. Highways 8, 53 and 63 and State Highways 25 and 48 cross it, and Rice Lake Regional Airport serves the area.

sections.h2: What should a seller have ready before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Gather the paperwork before the closing date so the recording does not hold up the sale. Most of the list comes straight from the sections above:

  • The signed, notarized deed with the full legal description. The DOR says the shortened description on a tax bill is not acceptable.
  • The parcel number from the Barron County tax bill.
  • The Real Estate Transfer Return receipt, or the exemption subsection if no fee applies.
  • Payment of the $30 recording fee and any transfer fee.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope or an email address for the return copy.

Ask the closing agent to confirm each item the day before closing.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Barron County?
faqs.a: Recording a deed in Barron County costs $30 under s. 59.43(2)(ag), Wisconsin Statutes. Subdivision, condominium and cemetery plats cost $50. The seller also owes the state transfer fee of $3 per $1,000 of value unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee?
faqs.a: The seller, who is the grantor on the deed, pays it. Section 77.22 puts the fee on the grantor at 30 cents per $100 of value. Both seller and buyer sign the transfer return, and the register collects the fee when the deed is submitted.

faqs.q: Does the Barron County Register of Deeds search titles for me?
faqs.a: No. The county's register page states that the office does not provide services for real estate searches. Ask your title company or closing agent to run the search, then bring the finished deed to the register to record.

faqs.q: Can a deed with a Social Security number be recorded?
faqs.a: No. Under s. 59.43(1m), a register of deeds may not record a document that contains an individual's Social Security number. Keep the number off the deed. The transfer return collects party identifiers separately through the Department of Revenue system.

faqs.q: How do I get my recorded deed back from Barron County?
faqs.a: Include a self-addressed stamped envelope for a paper copy or an email address for a PDF. The county page says recorded real estate documents are returned only when you provide one of these. Copies later ordered from the office cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page.
